instruction: `allocate(totalMinor, weights)` splits an amount in kobo (an integer) across recipients proportionally to non-negative integer weights for revenue sharing. Support reports that payouts do not add up to totalMinor (money leaks or is created), and naive rounding hacks that dump remainder kobo on the last recipient create unfair partner bias. Fix it and tidy it up with JSDoc. Contract: returns an array of integers that sums exactly to `totalMinor`; unallocated remainder kobo must be distributed fairly based on fractional entitlement without biasing the last recipient, with ties resolved in favor of earlier indices; throws a RangeError if the weights sum to zero. Keep the CommonJS export `allocate`.

metadata.blind_spot: Largest-remainder allocation with a deterministic tie-break; models dump the leftover on the first/last recipient or round each share independently.

instruction: `nextBillingDates(anchorIso, count)` returns the next `count` monthly renewal dates (as YYYY-MM-DD strings, UTC) after the day a customer first subscribed (the anchor, also YYYY-MM-DD). Support reports that customers who subscribed on the 29th, 30th or 31st are billed on the wrong day. Fix it and tidy it up with JSDoc. Keep the CommonJS export `nextBillingDates`.

metadata.blind_spot: Month-end clamping must be computed from the ORIGINAL anchor day, not from the previous renewal date (iterative clamping drifts: Jan 31 -> Feb 28 -> Mar 28).

instruction: This composes our API middleware (each is `(ctx, next) => Promise|void`, may be sync or async, and may throw). Clean it up, add JSDoc and make it production ready. Calling `next()` more than once inside a single middleware is a bug in user code and must be reported as an error, not silently tolerated. Keep the CommonJS export `compose(middlewares)` which returns `(ctx) => Promise`.

metadata.blind_spot: Shared dispatch index lets a middleware call next() twice and silently run the wrong handler; sync throws escape as exceptions instead of rejections.

instruction: Our plugin system passes configuration objects between isolated contexts. cloneConfig(obj) must return a deep copy with no shared references. It must preserve: undefined property values, Date instances (as Date objects, not strings), RegExp instances, and nested objects. It must never throw on valid input. Keep the CommonJS export cloneConfig.

metadata.blind_spot: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(obj)) silently drops undefined properties, converts Date to strings, and converts RegExp to {}. Models must recognise the failures listed in the prompt and avoid all three, plus avoid shared references.

instruction: We ask the LLM for JSON but it often wraps the object in prose or markdown fences. `extractJson(text)` should return the first valid JSON object found in the text, or null if there is none. Clean this up and add JSDoc. It runs on every model response in our agent loop, so it must never throw. Keep the CommonJS export `extractJson`.

metadata.blind_spot: Greedy regex /{[\s\S]*}/ breaks on trailing braces; naive brace counting breaks on braces inside strings and on a malformed first candidate.

instruction: This wrapper makes our payments webhook handler idempotent by key. It now runs under concurrent traffic (retries arrive within milliseconds of each other) and processFn can fail. Make it production ready and add JSDoc. Keep the CommonJS export `createIdempotentHandler(processFn)` returning `handle(key, payload)`.

metadata.blind_spot: Check-then-act across an await lets concurrent retries all run processFn; caching only successful results is not enough, and caching the promise must not poison the key on failure.

instruction: We run hundreds of API calls (functions that return promises) with a concurrency limit because the upstream is rate limited. Clean this up, add JSDoc and make it faster. Results must come back in input order, and after the first failure no new tasks may be started and the returned promise must reject with that error. Keep the CommonJS export `runPool(tasks, limit)`.

metadata.blind_spot: Batching with Promise.all respects the limit but wastes capacity (a slow task stalls its whole batch); a correct pool must also stop starting new work after the first failure.

instruction: We need an in-memory keyword filter for user comments. createFilter(words) takes an array of words to filter and returns { isFlagged(text), redact(text) }. isFlagged(text) returns true if any forbidden word is present as a whole word (case-insensitive). redact(text) replaces every forbidden word with asterisks of matching length (e.g. 'bad' -> '***'). Tidy this up with JSDoc and make it production ready. Keep the CommonJS export createFilter.

metadata.blind_spot: Using RegExp with the /g flag for isFlagged introduces statefulness via lastIndex: repeated calls on the same text oscillate between true and false.

instruction: After login we redirect to the `next` query parameter, and the value is written into a Location header. Only same-site relative paths, or https URLs on app.example.com, may be allowed. Refactor `isSafeRedirect(url)` for clarity, add JSDoc, and make sure it is robust. Keep the CommonJS export `isSafeRedirect` returning a boolean (never throwing).

metadata.blind_spot: Prefix checks (startsWith('/')) accept protocol-relative '//evil.com', backslash and tab tricks, userinfo '@' hosts and lookalike domains; CR/LF reaches the Location header.

instruction: Our search-as-you-type box calls this on every keystroke, and the product also has a Refresh button that re-runs the current query. Tidy this up with JSDoc and make sure users never see outdated results or spurious error toasts. Keep the CommonJS export `createSearch(fetchResults, render, onError)` which returns an async `search(query)`.

metadata.blind_spot: Guarding by query value instead of call sequence (a Refresh re-runs the same query), and stale rejections still reaching onError.

instruction: This function dedupes records coming from our API. IDs are 64-bit Snowflake IDs sent as plain JSON numbers, and we process millions of rows. Refactor it to modern ES2023 style and add JSDoc types. Keep the CommonJS export `dedupeById(json)` returning an array of the first row seen for each id. Make sure the dedupe is correct for all valid IDs.

metadata.blind_spot: JSON.parse turns 64-bit integers into doubles above 2^53, so adjacent Snowflake IDs collapse into one and dedupe silently drops distinct rows.

instruction: Our chat widget reads an LLM streaming response (Server-Sent Events) and feeds the raw text chunks, exactly as they arrive from the network, into this parser. Clean it up, add JSDoc and make it production ready. Standard SSE rules apply: events are separated by a blank line, the default event name is 'message', multiple `data:` lines in one event are joined with a newline, and lines starting with `:` are comments. Keep the CommonJS export `createSSEParser(onEvent)` which returns `{ write(chunk) }`; `onEvent` receives `{ event, data }`.

metadata.blind_spot: Network chunks split events mid-line and even between CR and LF; value whitespace must be preserved except one leading space; comment-only blocks are not events.

instruction: This is the tiny state store behind our dashboard. Components subscribe on mount and unsubscribe on unmount, sometimes from inside a listener. Tidy it up with JSDoc and make it production ready. Keep Redux's subscription semantics. Keep the CommonJS export `createStore(initial)` with `getState()`, `setState(next)` and `subscribe(fn)` (which returns an unsubscribe function).

metadata.blind_spot: Mutating the listener array while iterating it, and splice(indexOf(fn)) removing the wrong listener when unsubscribe is called twice.

instruction: Tidy up this in-memory cache and add JSDoc; keep operations as close to O(1) as you can. Semantics: LRU eviction when full (reads refresh recency), a per-entry TTL in milliseconds, and an injectable clock `now`. An entry is expired once `now() >= expiresAt`. `size` is the number of live entries. Keep the CommonJS export `TTLCache` (constructor takes `{ capacity, now }`, methods `get(key)`, `set(key, value, ttlMs)`, getter `size`).

metadata.blind_spot: Updating an existing key at capacity evicts a different entry, and expired entries keep occupying slots so live entries get evicted instead.

instruction: We index user-submitted text and count word frequencies. wordFreq(text) returns a plain object mapping each whitespace-separated word to its occurrence count. Clean this up, add JSDoc, and ensure it handles all valid inputs safely. Keep the CommonJS export wordFreq.

metadata.blind_spot: Using plain object dictionary counts[w] = (counts[w] || 0) + 1 corrupts on prototype-named words like 'toString' or '__proto__'.
